subject: Enterprise response windows, retainer options, and escalation coverage for Finosys
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@finosys.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finosys.com
Date: 2026-11-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA options for production go-live (need response windows + retainer pricing)

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the demo last week — Finosys is excited by Redwood's latency profile and the autoscaling behavior. We have a couple of firm asks as we prepare for procurement:

- Our platform needs a financial-grade uptime commitment for the critical inference path (we're evaluating 99.95 vs 99.99).
- We need 24/7 escalation coverage during business-critical hours for our fraud-detection pipeline (US/EU coverage).
- Looking for a short‑term retainer/priority support model that guarantees an on-call response window and direct escalation to engineering.

Can you send your standard uptime tiers, the cost delta for 99.99, and what a monthly retainer looks like (price and what it buys — response times, number of incidents, pager handoffs)? Procurement also asked for a sample MOU / commercial language to speed internal approvals.

Appreciate a one-pager and a ballpark by EOD tomorrow if possible.

Best,
Elena
Director of Platform Operations
Finosys

Attachments: none
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@finosys.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-01T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA options for production go-live (need response windows + retainer pricing)

Elena — thanks, and glad the demo landed. Short answer: we can support 99.95 and 99.99, and we offer two complementary premium support paths: a retainer-based Priority Support (guaranteed response windows, business-hour routing, and triage) and an Escalation Retainer for 24/7 engineering escalation.

I'll attach a simple one-pager with the tiers and price bands — see SLA_Tiers_v3.pdf (attached). High-level:
- Standard (included): 99.9 availability target, email support, standard SLOs.
- Priority (add-on): 99.95 target, 4-hour response for Sev1 during business hours, fast-track ticketing, recommended for higher throughput customers.
- Critical (add-on): 99.99 target, financial credits scale, 1-hour response during business hours, and optional 24/7 escalation retainer.

Retainer options (monthly):
- Priority Retainer: $8k/mo — covers up to 4 Sev1 incidents/month, 4-hour guaranteed response (BU hours), direct Slack channel, and two scheduled architecture-hours/month.
- Escalation Retainer: $25k/mo — 24/7 on-call escalation with 60-minute callback SLA, on-call rotation with access to senior engineering, and up to 8 incidents/month.

Discounting: for an annual commitment or >$200k ARR commit we can tier a discount (typical starting point: 12% on add-ons + 5% on seats).

I'll get Rishi to weigh in on the 24/7 rota and Jordan on escalation playbooks for the MOU language. Sending the MOU draft next.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA_Tiers_v3.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@finosys.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-01T17:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA options for production go-live (need response windows + retainer pricing)

Elena — quick technical note on what the retainer buys operationally:

- Priority Retainer (BU hours): direct routing to a dedicated TAM + escalation path to the on-call team. Response SLA = acknowledgment (phone/Slack) within 4 hours, initial mitigation guidance within 6 hours. No guaranteed engineering code changes in those windows — that comes with Escalation Retainer or a professional services engagement.
- Escalation Retainer (24/7): we provide a named escalation engineer and on-call rotation. Callback within 60 minutes, live conference bridge within 2 hours for Sev1 by default. For customers who require incident war-rooms, we add an incident facilitator fee per event (waived for first two incidents in month).

Operational notes: our 99.99 profile assumes multi-region redundancy and a small warm pool. If Finosys plans single-region heavy traffic, cost to maintain 99.99 will be higher (roughly +18–25% on Dedicated capacity). We can include a clause for cost-sharing for warm capacity if you want to optimize.

Happy to be on the call tomorrow to walk through traffic assumptions.

— Rishi
Director, Reliability & Support
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@finosys.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-02T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA options for production go-live (need response windows + retainer pricing)

Morning Elena — jumping in on the escalation process and commercial language for the MOU.

A couple of points we typically include:
1) Escalation queues and contact hierarchy (customer TAM -> on-call -> engineering lead -> exec on-call) with phone and Slack contact points.
2) Financial credits: tiered credit schedule tied to rolling 30-day availability with a cap at 50% of month charges for sustained outages (we can share exact figures in the MOU).
3) Incident allowance: retainer covers X incidents/month; anything beyond is billed at a per-incident rate.
4) Hotfix SLA vs. Engineering Work SLA — hotfixes prioritized during on-call; broader engineering work scoped and quoted separately.

Commercially, because Finosys is planning a multiregion deployment and has a multi-tenant critical path, our recommended package for pilot -> prod is: Priority Retainer for first 3 months while we stabilize (to ensure 4-hour response), then move to Escalation Retainer once you cross the 10M API call/month threshold. To support speedy procurement, I've attached a short MOU template with the contact hierarchy and credit table.

— Jordan
Head of Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MOU-Finosys-draft.docx
From: Elena Torres <elena@finosys.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finosys.com, David Park <david.park@acme-analytics.io>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA options for production go-live (need response windows + retainer pricing)

Thanks Hannah, Rishi, Jordan — helpful and thorough. A few clarifying Qs from procurement:

1) If we sign an annual commitment with Dedicated capacity, what is the effective discount on the Escalation Retainer?
2) For the Escalation Retainer, are on-call engineers in-region (US/EU) or time-shifted from Redwood's central rota? We need local-hours coverage for legal/regulatory reasons.
3) Can you confirm the credit calculation for a sustained 4-hour outage at 99.95 vs 99.99? Procurement wants a simple example in dollars.

We're aiming to have internal sign-off by next Friday. If you can confirm answers and send a DocuSign-ready MOU, procurement will fast-track it.

— Elena

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@finosys.com>, procurement@finosys.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA options for production go-live (need response windows + retainer pricing)

Elena — quick answers inline and next steps.

1) Discount on Escalation Retainer with annual Dedicated commit: typical structure is 15% off the retainer for 12‑month Dedicated capacity commits >= $300k, and 22% off for >= $600k. We can make that explicit in the MOU.

2) On-call coverage: we staff regional escalation engineers for US/EU for Escalation Retainer customers. Those engineers are local or time-zone aligned; we can list their locale in the MOU and include an SLA appendix listing in-region escalation as part of the retainer.

3) Credit example: assume monthly invoice = $100k (platform + retainer).
- At 99.95 (allowed downtime ~21.6 minutes/month), a sustained 4-hour outage exceeds the SLA. Typical credit = 10% of monthly charges for that window (example: $10k).
- At 99.99 (allowed downtime ~4.3 minutes/month), the same 4-hour outage typically triggers a larger credit (25% in our schedule) capped at 50% monthly charges (example: $25k, capped at $50k if charges were higher). Exact percentages are in the MOU credit table.

Next steps: I attached the MOU draft (MOU-Finosys-draft.docx) and created a DocuSign envelope link for the commercial terms — https://www.docusign.com/prepare/xyz-abc-123. If Finosys agrees to the Priority -> Escalation ramp and a 12-month Dedicated commit, we can get procurement-friendly language and a 15% retainer discount into the DocuSign today.

Would you like a 30-minute call now to finalize margins/discounts? Jordan and Rishi are on standby.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out quickly.

— Hannah
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0132

Attachments: SLA_Tiers_v3.pdf, MOU-Finosys-draft.docx
